Out at the moment but was tasked with this earlier on TG. 
I have a hot fix PR opened at work.ubq.fi to solve the UI problem immediately
I'd be grateful if you could assign or I will once back

I think this needs re-opened as the run isn't deleting issues ([run](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/actions/runs/10537424760/job/29198801008))
- it's trying to delete all issues from all bots
- it doesn't have correct access to delete issues
- [spam issues](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/issues/1334) still in the devpool
---
To delete an issue the `authToken` used must have admin permissions which I'm sure the bot does not have

- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/authentication/permissions-required-for-github-apps?apiVersion=2022-11-28
The app auth itself wouldn't be valid but if it's possible to give it admin permissions and then use it's token I don't see why that wouldn't work.
We might be able to do it by creating a fine-grained PAT with the resource owner being either the org or failing that then a user who has admin permissions. Scope it only to the `devpool-directory` repo with access to `issues` and `admin` on repo settings and idk if needed but `admin` on org too.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2821b01-7baf-481e-981e-a8193e1f06f3)
---
I expect that @jordan-ae will be required to resolve this considering a payout was made yeah? 
So what needs done is:
- create a new github app
- ensure that is given an `admin` role/permissions within the org
- Use the `authToken` from that app to delete the issues
- Ensure that the bot can delete and only unauthorized issues are removed
- Ensure that for in the case of forks, the contributor's issues don't get deleted
###### `/remindMe 1 day` ;)))

Resolves https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-bounties/issues/31
I QA'd the script manually locally and it works as expected. When using my PAT (with admin rights) issues are deleted. When using a different PAT it failed to remove any. Without the official instance env vars this was as close as I could get to fully testing it locally but I expect no issues.
- All issues created by my bot and `Keyrxng` were kept and any by my alt `Keyrxng2` were deleted.
- `GH_TOKEN` needs to be defined in secrets for this script to have the correct permissions.
- We authenticate as the `App` using the `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `APP_ID` so we can pull the installs. 
- We then map those to cover `User` and `Bot` types. If it's a bot we need to map the username to the `appSlug` as it's `userId` does not correspond to the `orgId` which it belongs to.
- For user's we map the `userId` directly.
While it's usually best to use numbers vs strings for identification this works just fine for identifying Bots as far as I could QA and was the best option I could think of given what was available.
---
In regards to future contributions we have two options:
1. Leave it as-is and forks need to define the correct secrets for this functionality to work
2. Don't throw for missing vars and without env vars we can assume this feature is disabled

comments.content:
There's already a similar issue https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-bounties/issues/30
@jordan-ae was the 1st one to pick it up so if he's still working on it then let's give him some time to self assign

This issue is pretty critical because it affects `work.ubq.fi` so either make sure your PR runs [locally](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/6c638ae0b21727962f92f25b4a79db2123ed9f52/.github/workflows/sync-issues.yml#L49) against your own `devpool-directory` repository without any errors either let @Keyrxng self assign it

Original [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-bounties/issues/30#issuecomment-2292647684) Right now anybody can create a new github issue in https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory and it will be displayed at `work.ubq.fi`: Allowing anybody to create issues in https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory is not optimal because: - anybody can flood `work.ubq.fi` with issues (illustrated on the screenshot above) - anybody can create a github issue with phishing URLs and that github issue will be displayed directly at `work.ubq.fi` One of the solutions could be to remove issues from https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory if they're opened not by one of the following bots (id => github URL): 1. `76412717: https://github.com/ubiquity` 2. `133917611: https://github.com/ubiquibot` 3. `165700353: https://github.com/UbiquityOS` P.S. There is also the [limit interaction](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/limiting-interactions-in-your-repository#about-temporary-interaction-limits) option but if we enable it then new contributors won't be able to open PRs towards https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory

@Keyrxng I've just QAed with an issue created by a user (by me actually) and the issue was deleted as expected https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/issues/1374.
Right now [GH_TOKEN](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/61045f468246a6fdde9901a400f0f9c1b348272f/.github/workflows/sync-issues.yml#L54) end variable is set to `0x4007`'s  PAT.  Do we keep using this PAT or we should create a separate github app with admin access to the https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory repository solely for deleting issues?

The solution with deleting unauthorized issues on "sync" still has a window for phishing since the sync workflow runs [once an hour](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/61045f468246a6fdde9901a400f0f9c1b348272f/.github/workflows/sync-issues.yml#L12) so an issue created by an adversary will be visible for a whole hour at `work.ubq.fi` in the worst case.
@0x4007 Are you ok with the approach that your github PAT is used for deleting issues?
What PR do you mean?
It its current view it doesn't solve the phishing issue

@Keyrxng What if we run [delete-unauthorized-issues.ts](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/61045f468246a6fdde9901a400f0f9c1b348272f/scripts/delete-unauthorized-issues.ts) in a separate workflow on `issues.opened`?
Why is that an issue?
https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-bounties/issues/35

I've just tried to use the bot's access token to delete [this](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/issues/1377) issue and got the `GraphQL: Viewer not authorized to delete (deleteIssue)` error in [this](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/actions/runs/10599106506/job/29373303161) CI run.
As [stated](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/deleting-an-issue) in the docs `Only accounts with admin or owner permissions can delete issues in a repository owned by an organization`. So although the `ubiquity-os` has read/write permissions for issues it can't delete them.
So we have 2 choices:
1. Use someone's PAT to delete issues
2. Simply close unauthorized issues by the bot

To sum up, as far as I understand, we have 2 account instances for managing https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory:
1. https://github.com/ubiquity-devpool: github account with the "owner" role [used](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/32f312e2b72fd15b447ab13264b85f3a0f1c342e/.github/workflows/sync-issues.yml#L54) for deleting unauthorized github issues
2. https://github.com/apps/devpool-directory-superintendent: github app [used](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/blob/32f312e2b72fd15b447ab13264b85f3a0f1c342e/.github/workflows/sync-issues.yml#L44) for opening and closing github issues

comments.content: @0x4007 Here you have results with the correct fetching of the linked pull-request. GraphQl is definitely more reliable to get this info.
There are two pull requests linked to this issue. One he is, one he is not. What should we do about it?

There is a different multiplier for `ISSUE_AUTHOR` and `PULL_AUTHOR` as well as `PULL_ASSIGNED` and `ISSUE_ASSIGNEE`.
Keyrxng is:
- `ISSUE_ASSIGNEE` on https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-bounties/issues/31
- `PULL_AUTHOR` on https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/pull/1341
- `PULL_COLLABORATOR` on https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/pull/1330
Which is why the second one rewards him. This would imply changing the whole logic to look at the originally assigned user to the issue from the PR and then consider the relationship to be `ISSUE_ASSIGNED` to override the `PULL_COLLABORATOR`. I do not know how v1 worked on this regard (with the bug it had it would reward everything regardless).

https://github.com/ubiquibot/conversation-rewards/issues/29#issuecomment-2222260068
I got rewarded for my comments on the PR, while I was assigned to the Issue and author of the PR, so I thought it was a normal scenario.
Then when checking the pull-request I will look back at its original issue and check if that person is assigned.

Pretty sure that the v2 always rewarded assignees of the issue but in 99% of them, the PR author was the same as the issue, so a multiplier of `0` was applied to both. Here is a rare case when multiple PRs and assigned users happened on the same issue.
